title: How to sort and classify tilesets well

posts.author: Angeling
posts.body: My problem with RPG Maker has always been sprites and tilesets, not for creating and designing them, but for how I classify them to implement them on a map, I use MZ and I'm experiencing problems with this. the amount of tilesets is limited, if I want to make an interior, for example "A4", "A1" and all that, I just want to place it on my map and that's it,

posts.author: SGHarlekin
posts.body:
Uhm, this is neither a tutorial, nor are you really asking any questions. This seems to be just a rant about you not understanding how it works?
Rpg maker has inbuilt tutorials for everything, there is a literal help file which has all the asset standards for you to look up and there's like a million mapping tutorials online.
So, whatever it is you need, it's 1 AI filled google search away.

posts.author: Danatoth
posts.body: Look into parallax mapping, it allows you to put whatever, wherever.

posts.author: MiguelRPG
posts.body:
I wish there were more tile sheets (F, G, H...), but the idea of using a single tileset for the entire project is bad on any platform, as it will make loading slower, consume more memory and the using it in the editor is difficult.
What I do in my projects to organize myself is separate the tiles that complement the structure in Tile B (walls, railings, cracks), the tiles that will always be repeated anywhere in Tile C (plants, flags, boxes... .) and Tile D and E be specific to the scenario (ship, house, bank, city center...)
Another point I see is that we are often making maps with many functions and that is why we lack tilesets, the map is a house, but in the middle there is a garden, which has a cave... it is possible that this is too much responsibility for the map, becoming heavy with events and boring because the player keeps walking in the same place.
